overall: The AG found violations for the July 14, 2021 meeting only: the notice's executive session topic was insufficiently detailed and the executive session discussion fell outside Purpose 6. No violation on the August and September meetings because no executive session was convened. Compliance ordered; no further remedy since minutes were released.

allegations.summary: July 14, 2021 notice listed only 'Executive Session – Donor Negotiations' and allegedly lacked sufficient detail on the executive session topic.
allegations.key_passage: As such, we find that the notice was insufficiently detailed with respect to the executive session topic.

allegations.summary: Commission allegedly entered executive session on July 14, 2021 for an improper purpose, discussing a monetary donation for a pickleball facility.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Commission violated the Open Meeting Law by entering into executive session for an improper purpose on July 14, 2021.

allegations.summary: August 11 and September 20, 2021 notices listed the same vague 'Donor Negotiations' executive session topic, allegedly lacking sufficient detail.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, because the Commission did not convene in executive session, we find no violation with respect to the sufficiency of the executive session topic listed on the notices.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Commission entered executive session on August 11 and September 20, 2021 for an improper purpose tied to the pickleball donation.
allegations.key_passage: With respect to the meetings held on August 11, 2021, and September 20, 2021, the Board did not convene in executive session on either date.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law (G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25).
remedy_passage: We order the Commission’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
